record_notes.DCP-LETT-1090: May 25, supplied 1847. Acknowledges the missing May 22 note, account and bank deposit; declines a summer Alford visit despite interest. Body amount £197 12 differs in precision from the editorial account-book entry £197 12s 10d dated May 26. Neither entry establishes the exact incoming delivery day. Prior 980 explains the banking arrangement, not this specific rent remittance.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1117: September 10, supplied 1847. Will allow Mason to buy rather than lease the small parcel, although he does not wish to sell; expects no expense. Asks about postal forgery, crossing drafts and the annual cost of two remittances. The catalogue summary says agrees to lease, but the body explicitly permits purchase if Mason prefers it. Higgins communication is implied by as you remark; absent. Earlier purchase papers 839/918 are not that request. No completed sale is established; 1377 later asks its outcome.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1138: December 11, supplied 1847. Acknowledges missing December 8 letter and account, reporting a future payment of £198 12s 3d, prosperous farm, unnamed old man death and kindness about Darwin father. The editor reconciles gross rent with £5 school subscription. Do not turn would pay into physical deposit proof or infer Robert Darwin death, which occurs the next year.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1159: February 28, supplied 1848. A missing letter from Mason requests half-yearly school payments on February 16 and August 16. Darwin asks Higgins to fit them around rent collection, then adds the option of retaining £5 at Lady Day. The source summary incorrectly says February 15. Modern footnote discussion of quarter-days is distinct from original wording. This initiates the surviving exchange answered by 1161; it cannot answer the later incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1161: March 1, 1848, surviving copy on 1159 according to XML. Higgins explicitly acknowledges the 28th ultimo and agrees to change payments from Michaelmas to Lady Day, leaving £2 10 in advance without retaining a cash balance. His view that Mason request is frivolous is Higgins voice. This is a reverse reply 1161→1159, not a Darwin target. Copy survival and dated reply establish Higgins knowledge of 1159 by March 1, not Darwin receipt or reading of 1161.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1184: June 6, supplied 1848 independently tied editorially to financial books. Missing June 3 note reports net bank draft; Darwin will tell his father about trust and Lord Yarborough, reports sister enjoyment of Lincolnshire and declines offered sea bathing. Susan report is oral/forwarded family information, not Higgins prose. Net £194 8s 1d reflects a £5 subscription deduction in the apparatus. Estate opportunity remains an editorial possibility, not an established transaction. Not an answer to March 1 subscription letter 1161.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1185: June 14, supplied 1848. Higgins missing June 8 letter was forwarded from Shrewsbury for Darwin decision. Will consider exchanging Sutterton for nearby land only if no income is lost after all sale, purchase and borrowing costs; strongly doubts feasibility. This is conditional assent, not completed sale or current title to Sutterton. Father ownership and subsequent inheritance are separate editorial context; 1211 later attests the inheritance. Specific June 8 input differs from 1161 and earlier estate papers.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1211: December 6, supplied 1848. Acknowledges missing bank-remittance note. Mourns father death, praises his kindness and reports that Sutterton Fen is left to Darwin, with rent due after November 13. Believes Salt wrote Higgins about rent to death date but is unsure what Salt communicated; do not turn that into a surviving letter or certain completed transmission. Original P3 wording is awkward and should not be silently repaired.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1243: June 5, supplied 1849, Malvern. Higgins June 1 letter was forwarded to Darwin at the place where he has stayed for health; acknowledges £216 2s 8d bank deposit. Neither the incoming letter nor forwarding/arrival day survives here. Older remittance or subscription letters cannot supply this prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1279: December 10, supplied 1849. Acknowledges missing December 8 letter and enclosures reporting £224 16s 5d deposited; regrets farmers gloomy prospects and possible rent reduction. Floods and corn-law debates are editorial possible explanations, not independently reported causes in Darwin text. No definite rent reduction is yet agreed in this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1326: May 9, supplied 1850. Accepts Higgins proposal of a 15 percent reduction for the past half-year, hopes depressed times temporary and compares prices under protection and in France. Asks whether Hardy works actively and has any complaint. Specific proposal is missing; 1279 is Darwin own earlier concern, not an incoming prompt. Editorial continuation of reduced income through 1852 is future knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1334: May 27, supplied 1850. Explicitly received Higgins letter and account this morning; separately advised by bankers of £183 5s 11d draft. Glad of good account of Hardy farming. These are two distinct communications; neither text survives. Exact morning receipt is supported for missing Higgins note, not for 1161 or all prior financial news.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1375: December 13, supplied 1850. Missing December 9 letter and account report £187 15s 11d draft. Regrets continued 15 percent reduction, hopes agricultural improvement and answers health inquiry. Prior outgoing 1326 establishes his agreement to reduction but is not an incoming letter. No more specific receipt date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1377: December 21, supplied 1850. Prospective nearly £5000 investment, asks land-market advice and moderate return; explicitly has not decided to buy. Family obligations motivate caution. Postscript cannot remember result of Mason proposed small-parcel purchase, connecting topic to 1117 without establishing any missing reply or completed sale. Expected source of funds from Emma trust is editorial inference, not body certainty. This opens an inquiry rather than answering the March 1848 note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-839: Prior context freshly reread: incomplete March 15, 1845 estate proposal ending mid-sentence; plan and particulars mentioned but not transcribed here. Approximate price £12500, 325 acres and expected clear return. Raw MathML gives 2½ miles and 3¼ percent, not 212 and 314. Later deposit and purchase identification in notes do not make them known at original composition. No current-period remittance or Mason request is contained here. No new or recounted prior edge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-918: Prior context freshly reread: October 2, 1845 improvements estimate, purchase cost, buildings and charges, expected rent and liquid-manure discussion. Son letter enclosed but missing; itemized enclosure not printed here. Hope to complete deeds October 10 is distinguished from editorial completion evidence. Raw MathML gives 3¼ percent. Flattened diag/ramme and separated cost rows need layout preservation, not ordinary prose. Original Darwin cover annotation dates papers October 1845 but does not fix the annotation or receipt day. No current-period prompt established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-980: Prior context freshly reread: May 27, supplied 1846 supported by account entry. Acknowledges rent draft, asks advance warning of building money, authorizes direct bank deposits, cannot meet in London and specifies roof pitch/oak lintels. Father temporarily short of money. Earlier building/rent business is relevant background but not a specific later remittance letter. Editorial Hardy identification is contractor Ralph, whereas current 1326 note identifies tenant Francis; do not merge them by surname.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1037: Prior context freshly reread: December 12, supplied 1846, acknowledges draft and farmhouse report, again requests direct rent payment to bankers and reports father recovering from illness. Missing corresponding note, not any new 1847–1850 incoming source. Planned visit next summer does not prove travel. Prior accepted relationships remain untouched.

reading_method: Independent fresh reading of 14 targets and four prior contexts, including full bodies, headers/XML, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly annotations and bibliography. Checked original fraction markup and financial table layout. No inline figures. Complete local Higgins identity inventory compared; no matching surviving current incoming letter for the acknowledged remittances.
